 petitioners.

versus
 State (Nct Of Delhi) And Anr.

Through: Mr.D.S.Dagar, APP f  with SI Ajay, PS Ne  Mr.Sunil Kumar Dixi  R2 with R2/complain  CORAM:
 HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE YOGESH KHANNA  ORDER % 16.02.2023 1.

Petitioners file this petition for quashing of the FIR No.367/2019 under Section 406/498A/34 Indian Penal Code registered at police station Neb Sarai, Delhi against them and the proceedings emanating therefrom.
2. The marriage between the petitioner No.1 and complainant/ respondent No.2 was solemnized on 14.04.2018 according to Hindu rites and ceremonies at Delhi.
No child is born from this wedlock.

However, due to matrimonial discord, couple started living separately from each other since 30.06.2019 and on the complaint of respondent No.2, the aforesaid FIR was registered against the petitioners.
The respondent No.2 also filed the complaint case under Section 12 of the DV Act.
During the pendency of proceedings, the couple settled the matter per settlement agreement dated 20.08.2022 before the Mediation Centre, Saket Courts.
The parties have also obtained divorce by mutual consent.

Pursuant to settlement, the petitioner No.1 agreed to pay Rs.15.50 Lacs to respondent No.2 towards all her claims of alimony, maintenance - past, present and future,
stridhan, and dowry articles etc.
3.

Out of said sum, the petitioner No.1 has already paid Rs.10.50 Lacs to respondent No.2 and for the balance amount, the petitioner No.1 has handed over draft No.279493 dated 14.02.2023 drawn Harish Rawat & Ors vs State (Nct Of Delhi) And Anr on 16 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/92704425/
1 on Union Bank of India for Rs.5.00 Lacs in favour of respondent No.2, which has been accepted by her.

entities.text: Harish Rawat & Ors vs State (Nct Of Delhi) And Anr
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 4. The complainant/respondent No.2 has been duly identified by the Investigating Officer, states the matter has been settled with the petitioners having left with no claim against them and she has no objection if the FIR is quashed.
The learned APP for the State has also no objection, if this petition is allowed.
The affidavits of parties are on record.

5. Considering the above settlement between the parties, there is no impediment in quashing of the FIR as complainant has settled all the disputes and has received the settled amount from the petitioners.
In view of the above, there is no use to continue with the proceedings against petitioners as it would never entail in conviction of petitioners.
6. Accordingly, the petition is allowed.
Consequently, FIR No.367/2019 under Section 406/498A/34 Indian Penal Code registered at police station Neb Sarai, Delhi and the proceedings emanating therefrom are quashed.
Pending application, if any, also stands disposed of.
No order as to costs.

YOGESH KHANNA, J.
FEBRUARY 16, 2023 M Harish Rawat & Ors vs State (Nct Of Delhi) And Anr on 16 February, 2023
